artifacts.summary: 6-phase implementation of the merge_targets.mcp deploy-engine mechanism, its regression harness, documentation, and the settled obsidian-memory resolution; all phases COMPLETED.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a merge_targets.mcp manifest key and deploy-engine dispatch branch (reusing the existing merge_settings/unmerge_settings primitive) so an extension can register a real MCP server into a project-scoped .mcp.json. Built a durable scratch-tree regression harness confirming all four requirements plus two empirical risk findings (byte-identity needed a sort_keys contingency; the regenerate-then-unload sequence reproduces a pre-existing, documented limitation). Documented the mechanism and its two user-visible gotchas, and resolved the absorbed obsidian-memory sub-task by removing its dead, fabricated server declaration and documenting Claude Code's native /ide integration as the real connection path.

memory_candidates.content: When reusing an existing additive-deep-merge primitive (merge_settings/unmerge_settings in this repo's extension deploy engine) for a NEW merge target, verify requirement (c) idempotency empirically rather than assuming it: jq .'s default behavior is order-preserving, not sorting, so a second deploy over already-merged content can fail a byte-identity check even though the content is semantically unchanged. The fix is an opt-in sort_keys flag threaded through write_json -> merge_settings, passed ONLY from the new branch, never changing any other caller's output format.

A load-call that OVERWRITES (rather than merges) its own previously-persisted merge-tracking data creates a latent 'load -> regenerate -> unload' retraction gap: a second load over already-present content produces a thinned tracked structure (deep_merge only tracks keys/items not already present), and since the persisted tracked data is replaced wholesale on each load, a later unload cannot retract entries that predate the most recent regenerate. This is a structural property of this repo's extension deploy engine (manager.load + state_mod.mark_loaded), shared by every merge-target branch (settings, mcp, ...), not specific to any one of them. A clean 'load -> unload' round trip with no intervening reload always retracts fully.

sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write and generate-context-line-counts.sh --write are repo-wide tools with no per-extension scope flag: running either during a multi-task /orchestrate batch cycle can silently write into a concurrently-dispatched sibling task's own declared file_scope (observed: registering a new test script in one extension's manifest also wrote missing-entry rows into an unrelated extension's manifest that a sibling task was actively editing). Always run `git diff --stat` immediately after invoking either tool in a batch context, and manually revert any hunk outside this task's own declared file_scope before committing -- never re-run a narrowing flag, because neither tool has one.
